title: I Posted the Community Garden Watering Roster the Chair Ignored

parts.text: I arrived at plot 14 at 6:10 a.m. with a watering can and found the chair's tomatoes on a soaker hose that had been running since Tuesday. The roster on the shed said rotate or lose the spigot. I was thirty-seven, third year on the waitlist before I got 14. My kale was dust. The chair, Bev, said leadership plots needed extra because of photos for the grant. I photographed the hose, the roster, the clock, and my kale. Then I printed the roster and zip-tied it to the spigot. At 6:24 a city inspector doing a drought check asked whose hose was the river.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The drought inspector is looking at Bev's soaker hose and the roster on the spigot.

social.video_title: Leadership tomatoes had a river — Part 1/2
social.description: Waitlisted kale, a Tuesday hose, a grant photo. The city arrived. Would you have zip-tied the roster?

parts.text: Bev shut the hose. The inspector logged a waste warning on the garden, not on a person, which is how cities talk. The board rotated the chair. I water 14 on my roster days. Bev waters 9 on hers. Grant photos now include a closed spigot. Kale recovered. Leadership is a plot number, not a river. The zip tie faded in the sun and I left it because faded rules still work.

social.video_title: The chair rotated and the spigot learned days — Part 2/2
social.description: Waste warning, plot 9, recovered kale. Was a grant a soaker hose?
